name: poll-widget

frames.best_why: Frame 3 shows an option selected with the submit button enabled, the clearest view of the poll.

tagline: Ask one question, take a vote, then thank the voter.
summary: An inline poll card with a question and four radio options. Choosing one enables a submit button; submitting plays a spinner and flips the panel to a centred success message naming the chosen option.
appearance: A dark panel holds a bold question, a muted line beneath it, and four stacked rounded rows, each with a small circular radio marker and a label. Under them sit a small vote count and a full-width submit button.
behaviour: Hovering lights a row's border. Clicking one fills its dot and turns the submit button from grey to white; submitting swaps the button for a spinner, then replaces the whole panel with a check and a short thank-you listing the option chosen.
demo_content: Options Faster build times, Better DX tooling, AI-assisted coding and Team collaboration.
search_phrases: quick poll to embed in a page
ask one question with radio buttons
vote and see a thank you message
inline survey with a submit button
use_when: You want a lightweight one-question vote embedded directly in the page rather than behind a click.
avoid_when: You need to show live results: after voting this switches to a thank-you card instead of a bar chart.
customise: The question, options, votes and callbacks are root props; the question, options, results and submit are assembled as child parts. Colours follow theme tokens.
weight_why: Four option rows, a couple of springs and short timers; no heavy rendering.

a11y.note: Option markers are aria-hidden and the success text replaces the form without a live region, so the result may go unannounced.

issues: The success card hides the poll and results, so voters never see the final percentages.
Frame 5 catches the transition with only a check icon and no text.
The disabled submit is very low contrast against the dark panel.
polish_why: Crisp rows and a satisfying success flip; the faint submit and missing results cost a little.
